text:
maria_cs: Hey team, we got a customer report: mobile app sees partial JSON payload from SSE, then on quick reconnect the server sent a short tail that duplicated the last paragraph. Customer says they were double-billed for ~12 tokens. Can we triage?

priya_support: Thanks — customer gave a timeline and sample client logs. They see SSE disconnected at ~08:13:21, client retried immediately with the same request id, and got an extra chunk that repeated the previous sentence. They attached app logs (snippet).

sam_engineer: Can you paste the client logs and the server correlation id? Need to see resume_token and sequence numbers. Often dupes happen when client retries without idempotency token or we accept two concurrent sessions during short port reuse.

maria_cs: Correlation id: rwd-ctx-9f2d4. Client log: ``[08:13:21] sse: disconnected (WS code 1006)
[08:13:21.110] sse: reconnecting, reusing requestId=10f-req, resume_token=resume:eyJhIjoxfQ==
[08:13:21.145] sse: received chunk {"seq":42,"text":"...the quick brown fox."}
[08:13:21.210] sse: received chunk {"seq":43,"text":"the quick brown fox."}``

sam_engineer: Ok sequence numbers 42 then 43 where 43 is the same sentence appended. Server logs for rwd-ctx-9f2d4 show: ``[runtime] accepted resume token resume:eyJhIjoxfQ== for session s-7fa, last_seq=42, kv_nonce=abc123
[inflight] launching new session s-7fb for request 10f-req (port rebind)
[billing] counted tokens for session s-7fb: 12 tokens
[runtime] emitted chunk seq=43 text=\"the quick brown fox.\"
[audit] audit-id a7: duplicate output detected by client ack mismatch``

evan_runtime: That log is interesting — it shows two sessions (s-7fa and s-7fb) were both active for short period. We have a known edgecase when resume tokens are accepted even if the server's kv cache nonce differs (port/connection reuse allowed resume), which can cause duplicate tail emission when client does an immediate retry. We usually validate resume token + last_seq against an active session nonce. Looks like nonce mismatch check was permissive here which allowed a stale resume to be accepted and we replayed final chunk.

priya_support: Customer says they called immediately after disconnect and client retries automatically with the same idempotency.key (they reuse requestId). They expected idempotency to prevent duplicate generation.

sam_engineer: Two problems colliding: 1) client reused requestId but our current idempotency semantics for streaming + resume only dedupe identical complete requests, not incremental resumed sessions. 2) resume acceptance path accepted a stale resume_token when the kv_nonce didn't match, so we emitted the tail from the original session. Combined equals duplicated content + billing charge.

maria_cs: Action items? Customer wants a credit and a patch.

evan_runtime: Immediate mitigation for CS: ask customer to set client to wait 200-500ms before retrying OR rotate a new request-level idempotencyKey on reconnect attempts. We'll issue a temporary credit once we confirm billing records. For longer term: we'll tighten resume validation to require matching kv_nonce OR attach a resume-scoped nonce check in the token. Also we should change billing to only charge on first finalization ack from the authoritative session.

sam_engineer: Attached quick repro for eng to reproduce locally (SSE client using curl + python):
```
# reproduce: simulate disconnect then immediate reconnect using same requestId
curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "X-Request-Id: 10f-req" \
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=test-compact" | sed -n '1,200p'
# Or python snippet to force port reuse and immediate reconnect
import requests, time
hdrs={"Accept":"text/event-stream","X-Request-Id":"10f-req","Resume-Token":"resume:eyJhIjoxfQ=="}
r=requests.get('https://local-runtime/stream', headers=hdrs, stream=True)
for chunk in r.iter_lines():
    print(chunk)
    if b'quick brown fox' in chunk:
        # simulate sudden disconnect
        r.close()
        # immediate reconnect
        r2=requests.get('https://local-runtime/stream', headers=hdrs, stream=True)
        for c in r2.iter_lines():
            print(c)
        break
```

evan_runtime: I can reproduce with a local runtime using port-reuse fast reconnect and a patched accept_resume handler. Repro steps show two sessions briefly accepted; the second session was charged because billing increments on emitted tokens.

jules_billing: If we can get the audit-id (a7) and customer account id, we can look up the charge. If duplicate tokens are present within a 5s window for the same requestId/resume-token pair, we can issue a targeted credit. Please include the server logs and the full timeline.

maria_cs: I have the account id (acct_76Z). Sending logs to billing now.

priya_support: Temporary workaround we gave customer: enable client-side `sse.retryDelayMs=300` and ensure new idempotencyKey on reconnect. Also suggested they send final ack from client when they see end-of-stream to avoid automatic immediate retry. They applied retryDelay and reported no dupes during 30m test.

sam_engineer: Proposed runtime bugfix: 1) tighten resume acceptance to require kv_nonce equality OR a short-lived resume-grant token tied to session. 2) make token emission atomic: on resume acceptance server should compute delta and only send missing chunks (dedupe by seq) and reject resume that would cause overlap. 3) change billing to mark tokens provisional until finalization ack, then confirm charge; if a second concurrent session emits same seq we do not double-charge.

evan_runtime: Filed ENG-REPRO-1142 and assigned to eng-runtime. I'll add unit tests that simulate NAT port reuse and immediate reconnect.

maria_cs: Thanks. Priya will follow up with credit and instructions. Putting this thread in follow-up queue. :white_check_mark: 

oncall-bot: Incident link created: https://redwood.ai/incidents/ENG-REPRO-1142 — assigned to evan_runtime.

priya_support: Closing loop with customer: "we've issued a partial credit of X tokens while engineering rolls out a fix; for now please keep retryDelay >=300ms or rotate your request id per reconnect."

sam_engineer: Note for internal doc: add a short section in SSE troubleshooting about port reuse + resume_nonce mismatch causing tail-append duplicates and suggested client-side mitigations.

maria_cs: I'll add the KB note and attach repro gist. Thanks everyone.
